item.title: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
item.description:
Europe
French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
November 27, 20266:49 AM ET
By
The Associated Press
FILE - Actor Gerard Depardieu arrives to face trial for the alleged sexual assaults of two women on a film set in 2021, on March 24, 2025 in Paris.
Aurelien Morissard/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Aurelien Morissard/AP
PARIS — Gérard Depardieu, for decades one of France's most celebrated actors, has been ordered to stand trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting a young actress, authorities said Thursday, less than two weeks after the cinema star abandoned his appeal of a sexual assault conviction in a separate case.
Actress Charlotte Arnould was 22 when she accused Depardieu in 2018 of raping her at his Paris home.
Eight years later, the Paris Court of Appeal ruled that the actor should face trial over allegations of rape and sexual assault on Aug. 7, 2018, while dismissing allegations relating to a second incident six days later.
Depardieu, 77, has denied the rape allegations. His lawyer, Delphine Meillet, told The Associated Press that he disputes Thursday's ruling, without specifying whether he would challenge it before France's highest court for civil and criminal cases.

item.title: Screen free tweens try their hand at Dungeons & Dragons
item.description:
K-12 Education
Screen free tweens try their hand at Dungeons & Dragons
November 27, 20265:00 AM ET
Sequoia Carrillo
First published in 1974, Dungeons & Dragons is now being embraced by a new generation looking for a screen-free hobby.
Lauren Migaki/NPR
hide caption
toggle caption i
Lauren Migaki/NPR
Dungeons & Dragons has captivated players for more than fifty years.
In its early days, some parents complained that the role-playing game kept kids holed up inside for hours at a time. NPR even did a 10 minute piece on it in 1979. In recent years, D&D has come back into popular culture through shows like Stranger Things, a 2023 blockbuster movie and an influx of interest during the COVID-19 lockdowns.
Now, what was once a nerdy pastime has become a screen-free parent's dream – a game that relies on imagination, a role of the dice and in-person communication.

item.title: Eagles rally to stun Cowboys coming back from 21 points behind
item.description:
Sports
Eagles rally to stun Cowboys coming back from 21 points behind
November 27, 20263:23 AM ET
By
The Associated Press
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Joe Milton III (14) runs against the Dallas Cowboys in the second half during an NFL football game in Arlington, Texas, Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026.
Julio Cortez/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Julio Cortez/AP
ARLINGTON, Texas — Joe Milton rolled to his left while motioning DeVonta Smith where to go near the end zone, then threw the kind of deep ball the Dallas Cowboys always knew he was capable of when he was playing for them.
That 50-yarder was the first of two long touchdowns for the Philadelphia duo against the quarterback's former team, and the start of quite a comeback.
Milton, who was Dak Prescott's backup all last season, threw three touchdowns and ran for another one in a 39-38 win Thursday in his third start for the Eagles, who signed him off the Dallas practice squad on Oct. 16.
"The guy's a rock star. ... True example of being cool, calm, collected, and just keep playing the next play, no matter what the outcome," said Eagles tackle Jordan Mailata, who was then asked about the long TD passes. item.title: Strobe Talbott, former Time magazine reporter and deputy secretary of state, has died
item.description:
Obituaries
Strobe Talbott, former Time magazine reporter and deputy secretary of state, has died
November 27, 20261:12 AM ET
By
The Associated Press
FILE - Strobe Talbott, President Brookings Institution, speaks during a news conference in Berlin, July 16, 2008.
Franka Bruns/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Franka Bruns/AP
Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as deputy secretary of state under President Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday. He was 80.
His son, Devin Talbott, confirmed he passed away peacefully after a long illness in his East Hampton, New York, home.
The elder Talbott was educated at Yale and Oxford, where he bunked with Clinton. While at the British university, after interning for Time in Moscow, the magazine asked Talbott to help translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev, the former first secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union who was ousted in 1964.
